 This Motor Accident Claims Appeal Having Been Finally Heard
On 27.03.2026, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 M.A.C.A.No.1261 of 2016

Jacob vs Santo K.T on 27 March, 2026

This appeal has been preferred by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation amount awarded in O.P. (MV).No.1272/2011 of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda, and also challenging the finding of the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and the consequent reduction in the award amount.
2. Claimant filed the petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, stating that on 11/07/2011 at about 7.30 p.m, while he was riding a scooter bearing registration No.KBR-1034 through Angamali-Chalakudy road and when he reached at Chirangara, a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-45/E 8661 ridden by R1 in a rash and negligent manner hit on his scooter and in the said accident, he sustained serious injuries.
Accident occurred due to 2026:KER:28270 the rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by R1, who was the owner cum rider of the said vehicle.
R2 is the insurer.
3. Before the Tribunal, R1 remained ex parte.

4. R2 filed written statement admitting the insurance policy for the motorcycle, but it was contended that at the time of accident claimant had no driving license and the accident occurred due to the inexperienced driving of the claimant.
It was further contended that the final report filed by the police in the said crime would also show that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.
It was also contended that the compensation claimed under the different heads are excessive.

5. After trial, the learned Tribunal assessed the compensation of Rs.3,07,115/-, but 40% of the said amount was deducted on the ground that the claimant who had no driving licence also contributed to the accident and therefore, he is entitled to get only Rs.1,84,269/- with interest at the rate of 8%
per annum.

6. Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation and also aggrieved by the finding that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant, this appeal has been preferred by the claimant,
contending that the finding of the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant is a wrong finding; that the Tribunal failed to take note of the fact that 1st respondent, who was the rider of the motorcycle, pleaded guilty before the learned Magistrate, whereas the claimant herein, who was charged was acquitted of the charges levelled against him.

It was further contended Jacob vs Santo K.T on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79892374/
2 that the finding of the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and the consequent reduction of 40% of the award amount assessed is illegal.
The claimant also contended that the amount awarded by the Tribunal under various heads are meager and inadequate and it is not a just compensation as mandated in law.

7. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurance company contended that the claimant who was riding the scooter bearing registration No.KBR-1034 at the time of the accident 2026:KER:28270 had no driving licence and there was contributory negligence on his part.
8. It is an admitted fact that on 11.07.2011, the claimant met with a motor vehicle accident.

It is in evidence that the scooter ridden by the claimant and the motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-45/E 8661 ridden by R1 collided at Chirangara and in the said accident, claimant sustained injuries.
9.
Ext.A1 is the FIR registered qua the accident.
There was 'A' charge and 'B' charge.
Ext . A2

is the 'A'
charge and Ext.A12 is the 'B' charge.

Ext.A4 is the judgment in C.C.No.1676/2011 of JFCM,
Chalakudy dated 21.12.2011 in respect of 'A' charge.
Ext .A13 is the judgment in C.C.No.7076/2012 of JFCM, Chalakudy in respect of 'B' charge.
A perusal of Exts.A2 and A4 would show that R1 pleaded guilty to the charge against him under Sections 279 and 338 IPC and he was convicted.

Exts.A12 and A13 would show that claimant herein who was charged under Sections 279 and 338 IPC was found not guilty for the offences under Sections 279 and 338 IPC and he was acquitted of the said offences under Section 255(1)(c) Cr.P.C.
2026:KER:28270 10.
Thus, the claimant was found not guilty by a competent court.
The contention of the learned counsel for the R2/insurance company is that the claimant had no valid driving licence at the time of the accident.
Even if the claimant had no valid driving licence at the time of accident, that by itself is not a ground to hold that he was negligent and his rashness and negligence resulted in the accident.
There is no evidence to show that there was any contributory negligence on the part of the claimant, which caused the accident.

11. Driving without a licence is a violation of Motor Vehicles Act, but it does not mean that claimant was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and there was contributory negligence on his part.
12. Insurance company failed to prove that the lack of driving licence for the claimant caused the accident and there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant.

13. In Sudhir Kumar Rana vs Surinder Singh & Ors [(2008) 12 SCC 436] and Srikrishna Kanta Singh vs The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. [2025 SCC OnLine SC 636], the Hon'ble 2026:KER:28270 Supreme Court held that the driving without licence is an offence but it cannot be the sole basis to render a finding that there was contributory negligence on his part.

3 14.

It is a well settled principle that for a deduction to be made on the ground of contributory negligence, there should be evidence to prove that the victim, who suffered injury or death was driving rashly and negligently and it contributed to the accident.
Driving without a licence does not automatically lead to a presumption of contributory negligence.
There is no evidence to show that the lack of licence for the claimant was the reason for the accident.
Driving without licence does not automatically lead to the conclusion that there was contributory negligence.

Hence the finding of the learned Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and 40% is to be deducted from the amount assessed as damages is untenable and no reduction can be made from the awarded amount.
15. Now let us see whether the claimant is entitled to get enhanced compensation.
Ext.A3 wound certificate would show that claimant sustained deep wound over the parieto occipital region and diffuse sub arachnoid haemorrhage.
Medical records, namely Ext.A8 discharge summary issued from the hospital would show that he was treated as an inpatient at that hospital on 11.07.2011 and discharged on 08.08.2011.
The medical records would further reveal that the injured has developed chest infection.
He was again admitted on 13.09.2011 and discharged on 17.09.2011.

Ext.A10 is the disability certificate issued by the doctor, wherein it has been started that on account of the injuries sustained the claimant suffered 16.70% disability and the Tribunal took the percentage of disability as 10%.
17.
According to the claimant, he was working as two wheeler mechanic cum driver of a garage named 'Royal Garage', Angamaly, and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

To substantiate his case that he was a two wheeler mechanic cum driver of 'Royal Garage' he has produced Ext.A11 salary certificate to the effect that he was drawing a monthly salary of 2026:KER:28270 Rs.10,000/-.
The Tribunal has taken Rs.6,000/- as notional income.

18. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that going by the decision of the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the Tribunal ought to have taken at least 8,000/- per month as notional income.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. In Ramachandrappa [cited supra], the Hon'ble Supreme Court fixed the notional income of a coolie worker in the year 2004 as 4,500/- per month.

In Syed Sadiq and Others v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd. [(2014) 2 SCC 735] the Hon'ble Supreme Court fixed the notional income of a vegetable vendor in the year 2008 at the rate of 6,500/- per month.

entities.text: Syed Sadiq and Others v. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.Ltd. [(2014) 2 SCC 735]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
20. In National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others [(2017) 16 SCC 680] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the principle that there would be incremental enhancement in the case of even self-employed individuals in the 2026:KER:28270 unorganized sector and with respect to an unspecified job of a coolie considering the increase in cost of living and economic advancement over the years, it can be safely assumed that even a coolie worker would be eligible for incremental addition of 500/- in every subsequent year.

4 21.

sentences.text: Bearing in mind the above yardsticks, this Court is of the view that the notional monthly income of the claimant who is a two wheeler mechanic cum driver occupation can be fixed at 8,000/- per month for the purpose of assessing the compensation payable in the claim petition filed by him.
Therefore, under the head loss of earnings, he is entitled to get an amount of 24,000/- [8,000x3].
22. Ext.A10 is the disability certificate, wherein the Medical Board has assessed his whole body disability as 16.70%.
Claimant was aged 57 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to him is 9.
Accordingly, under the head permanent disability an amount of 1,44,288/- is awarded (8,000x12x9x16.70/100).
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads found to be just and reasonable and therefore needs no interference.
24. In the result M.A.C.A stands allowed with costs.

The compensation payable to the appellant/claimant is as indicated in the tabular statement here below:

(8,000x3)
2. Transportation expenses 2,000/- 2,000/-
3.

Extra Nourishment 5,000/- 5,000/-
4. Damage to clothing 500/- 500/-
5.

Bystander expenses 5,000/- 5,000/-
6.

Medical expenses 1,61,815/- 1,61,815/-
7.

Pain and suffering 25,000/- 25,000/-
8.

Permanent disability 64,800/- 1,44,288/-
9.

Loss of amenities 25,000/- 25,000/-
 Loss of earning power

5  Total 3,07,115/- 3,92,603/-
Amount enhanced  85,488 (3,92,603-3,07,115)
25.
Respondents are jointly severally liable to pay the award amount of 3,92,603/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
R3 insurance company shall deposit the award amount within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after deducting the deposit if any already made.
Since there was a delay of 35 days in filing the appeal, the appellant/claimant will not be entitled to interest on the enhanced amount for the period of 35 days.

27. The appellant shall produce the details of the bank account before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda, within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
